title: A Portrait for the Letter
premise: Ada Oyelaran, the night dispatcher who has quietly catalogued two decades of Hollowmere's secrets, receives a prepaid booking from a stranger asking to be driven to a house where a murder is scheduled — and to prove it never happens. The 'victim' is Nell Barrow, a woman officially declared dead three years ago, whose survival everyone in power depends on denying. As Ada traces Nell through her own archived call logs, she uncovers that the town's beloved benefactor built his fortune on the fire Nell was supposed to die in. In the end Ada must choose between burning her twenty years of careful invisibility by testifying, or letting Nell vanish again; she chooses truth, trading her anonymity for justice and finally stepping out of the filing cabinet of her own life.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen spent fifteen years as a court stenographer in northern England before turning to fiction, a career that taught her how much people reveal when they think no one is writing it down. She writes mysteries about quiet women who notice everything, and lives near the coast with an untidy archive of her own making.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Ada. A cash envelope arrives at the dispatch office: payment for a future ride to 14 Calder Row, with instructions to confirm a murder does not occur there. The emotional beat is unease — Ada's instinct to file and forget collides with the fact that someone knows exactly how she works.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She searches her private ledgers for Calder Row and finds Nell Barrow's name — logged as deceased three years ago, yet with calls placed after the death date. The beat is dread mixed with the thrill of a pattern only she can see.

chapters.title: A Woman Officially Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Nell's POV. Nell, living under another name, realizes someone has been asking about her and prepares to run again. The beat is paranoia mirrored: hunter and hunted both checking the same locks at night.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Digging into the town archive, she connects Nell's 'death' to the warehouse fire that launched philanthropist Edmund Voss's fortune. The beat is cold clarity — corruption dressed as charity, and Ada realizing how deep her own employer's silence runs.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Files
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her ledgers are disturbed; her supervisor warns her off, gently, then not gently. The beat is fear sharpening into defiance — invisibility, her armor for twenty years, is being stripped away.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell reaches out through the taxi company, testing whether Ada is bait or ally. A tense midnight meeting in the depot yields partial trust. The beat is fragile connection between two women who have survived by staying unseen.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Nell reveals she witnessed Voss lock the doors before the blaze; the 'murder' the client paid to disprove is the one he plans to finish now that she's resurfaced. The beat is grief and resolve — the past was never buried, only filed.

chapters.title: The Ride to Calder Row
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The prepaid fare comes due: Voss's man forces Ada to drive Nell to 14 Calder Row herself, believing she'll comply out of fear. The beat is terror transmuted into cunning — Ada uses her knowledge of routes, dead zones, and dispatch codes to turn the trap around.

chapters.title: Every Call Recorded
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At Calder Row, Voss confronts them, but Ada has broadcast the whole exchange over the open dispatch channel — every patrol officer, every night worker, listening. The beat is cathartic exposure: the invisible woman makes the town witness everything at once.

chapters.title: Out of the Filing Cabinet
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue tone. Nell testifies; Voss falls; Ada gives her first-ever statement under her own name and takes a daylight job training new dispatchers. The beat is quiet triumph — loyalty to truth cost her invisibility and bought her a life.
